# Claude Code Environment Variables: Tools and Bash

These 109 environment variables of Claude Code `2.1.303` cover the `Bash` tool, file tools, search, permissions, and the sandbox.
They set time limits, output limits, and safety switches for the tools.
An environment variable is a named setting that you put in your shell or in the `env` key of `settings.json`.

## Example

Run `export BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000` before `claude` to let a `Bash` command run for five minutes.
Or put `{ "env": { "BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS": "300000" } }` in `~/.claude/settings.json`.

## Variables

The marks are explained on the [index](Claude-Code-Env-Vars#marks).

| `SHELL` | ✅ | Names the user shell. Claude Code uses it to find tools, to describe the shell in the prompt, and to run login-shell probes. | Text. Non-empty string. Falls back to `/bin/zsh` for one probe and to `unknown` in the prompt text | All sessions, Windows sets it itself |
| `SUDO_GID` | 🔍🧪 | Group id of the user who ran `sudo`. Claude Code uses it with `SUDO_UID` and `SUDO_USER` to find the real user when it runs as root. | A number. Integer, digits only, min `0`. Used only when the process uid is `0` | Linux and macOS as root |
| `SUDO_UID` | 🔍🧪 | User id of the user who ran `sudo`. Claude Code uses it to decide who owns files and git repos when it runs as root. | A number. Integer, digits only, min `0`. Used only when the process runs as root | Linux and macOS as root |
| `SUDO_USER` | 🔍🧪 | Name of the user who ran `sudo`. Claude Code checks it against the system and uses it as the real owner when it runs as root. | Text. Non-empty string that must match a safe name pattern. Used only as root | Linux and macOS as root |
| `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` | ✅❌ | Does nothing now. Docs say it was removed in v2.1.277 together with the `TaskOutput` tool. | - | All sessions |
| `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP` | ✅ | Set to `0` to use the system `rg` instead of the bundled one. | On or off. Project settings may set it before trust (allowlist true) | All sessions. Project `env` can set it before trust |
